title: Spike: TanStack Start on Workers reaching the API via Service Binding
content:
Throwaway code. The two-repo split is only cheap if Service Bindings work from TanStack Start server functions.

Must answer:
- Does TanStack Start deploy to Workers cleanly with wrangler?
- Can a server function reach a Service Binding, or only the fetch handler?
- Does SSR streaming survive the binding call?
- How is the binding typed and configured across two wrangler.toml files?

If server functions cannot reach the binding, the split costs a real network hop on every render and hosting should be reconsidered.

title: Bootstrap sebp-api repository
content:
Hono on Workers, empty but fully wired.

- pnpm, TypeScript strict, Hono, Zod, Drizzle, wrangler
- vitest with @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers, isolated storage per test
- Coverage thresholds at 100% (lines, functions, branches, statements)
- ESLint with no-restricted-imports and no-restricted-globals per codebase-structure.md §14
- dependency-cruiser config enforcing domain purity, barrel-only cross-module imports, better-auth confinement, no cycles
- Directory skeleton per §2, empty modules
- dev/staging/production environments with separate D1, R2, KV, Queue bindings

Done when: pnpm lint && pnpm depcruise && pnpm test all pass on an empty repo, and a hello-world route is deployed to dev.

title: Bootstrap sebp-web repository
content:
TanStack Start on Workers, empty but fully wired. Depends on the Service Binding spike.

- pnpm, TypeScript strict, TanStack Start, wrangler
- Playwright with Istanbul instrumentation of the built bundle and coverage merge
- Coverage threshold at 100%
- Route group skeleton: (public), (auth), (app), (admin)
- lib/api/client.ts as the only API caller; lib/api/generated/ wired to openapi-typescript
- Service Binding to sebp-api configured

Done when: a public SSR page renders meaningful HTML with JavaScript disabled, one Playwright test passes at 100%, deployed to dev.

title: Platform ports and composition root
content:
The seam every other module depends on. No business logic.

Ports in src/ports/: Clock, IdGenerator, ObjectStorage, KeyValueStore, JobQueue, Notifier — signatures per codebase-structure.md §6, all returning Result.

Adapters in src/platform/: R2ObjectStorage, KvStore, CfJobQueue, PingramNotifier, systemClock, uuidV7Generator. Drizzle client for D1.

shared/: Result type and helpers, branded id types, error unions.

container.ts constructing all of the above from Env.

Done when: dependency-cruiser passes, the container builds in a test, and each adapter has a failing-path test using port substitution.

title: CI pipeline with the three gates
content:
GitHub Actions for both repos: pnpm lint && pnpm depcruise && pnpm test, failing on coverage below 100%.

Also: migrations applied in CI, wrangler deploy to dev on merge to main, and openapi-typescript regeneration checked in sebp-web so a stale client fails the build.

title: Spike: better-auth on Workers with a Drizzle D1 adapter
content:
Throwaway code. Prove better-auth actually runs on Cloudflare Workers backed by D1 through Drizzle.

Must answer:
- Does the Drizzle D1 adapter work, or does it assume node/postgres?
- Email + password signup, email verification, phone OTP — all supported?
- What schema does it own, and how does it collide with startups.owner_user_id?
- Session validation cost per request — does it hit D1 every time?
- Password hashing: bcrypt is unavailable in Workers. What does it use?

Deliverable: a working throwaway Worker plus a short written verdict in the task comment. If it does not work, say so loudly — the entire identity design depends on it.

title: Spike: verify Pingram's API surface
content:
Confirm against Pingram's own documentation, not assumption.

Must answer:
- Auth model and how the key is held in Workers secrets
- OTP support for phone verification, or must we build it
- SMS coverage in applicant regions
- Delivery webhooks for bounce and failure — payload shape, signature verification
- Rate limits and pricing at expected volume

The Notifier port shape (§8.3) depends on this. No delivery webhooks means notification_deliveries status tracking cannot work.

title: Vertical slice: rounds, end to end
content:
One module proving every pattern before the other eight are written. Deliberately narrow: create a round, list rounds, read one.

Exercises the whole stack — migration, Drizzle schema, domain entity with Result, repo port and D1 adapter returning domain entities, query port returning read-model DTOs, use-case, thin route with Zod, OpenAPI entry, container wiring, e2e tests through HTTP at 100%, deployed.

Done when:
- POST /api/v1/admin/rounds and GET /api/v1/admin/rounds work against real D1
- /openapi.json includes them, generated from the same Zod schemas
- Coverage is 100% with no v8 ignore hints
- All three gates green, deployed to dev
- A written note in the task comment on where the 100% gate hurt — that finding shapes the other eight modules

title: Define the complete database schema
content:
Turn technical-design.md §4 into concrete, complete DDL before any code depends on it. Produces docs/data-model.sql plus a short notes file — not Drizzle code, since neither repo exists yet. Bootstrap translates it afterwards.

Scope — every table in §4:
- rounds, stage_definitions, stage_transitions_config
- field_definitions, field_values
- document_requirements, document_submissions, document_identities
- applications, application_stage_instances, stage_transition_log
- notification_templates, notification_triggers, notifications, notification_deliveries
- events, event_registrations
- announcements, announcement_reads
- support_tickets, support_messages
- audit_log
- startups (ours) — see the identity boundary note below

For each table: every column with type, nullability and default; primary and foreign keys with cascade behaviour; every index; every constraint.

Must get right:
- round_id scoping on every scoped table, per §4.2. A definition query without a round_id is a bug waiting to happen.
- Locale-keyed JSON columns for all admin-editable labels — stage/field/document names, help text, notification templates (§10).
- The duplicate-gate partial unique indexes (§7.5): global scope and round scope are different constraints on document_identities, over value_normalised, not value_raw.
- Generated columns and expression indexes for dynamic-field filtering (§13.3). Define the mechanism; do not pre-index every field.
- append-only configuration: archived_at everywhere, and unique constraints that ignore archived rows.
- audit_log carries no PII (§4.9). Verify no column can hold a name, email, or document content.

Identity boundary: better-auth owns users, sessions, account and verification. Define only what we own — startups.owner_user_id referencing better-auth's user id. Mark the exact seam and leave it provisional; TASK-39 confirms the real shapes.

D1/SQLite specifics to resolve, not assume:
- Foreign key enforcement behaviour in D1 and whether a PRAGMA is needed
- Partial unique index support for the WHERE archived_at IS NULL pattern
- Generated column support and STORED vs VIRTUAL trade-offs
- No native jsonb — confirm the json_extract approach performs acceptably

Done when: the DDL applies cleanly to a local D1, every table in §4 is present, a reviewer can trace each column back to a section of the technical design, and any deviation from that document is either fixed there or justified in the notes.
